hero.name: Danil Zablotsky
hero.statement: I design interfaces and build them myself, all the way to working products on iOS, Android and the web.

story.title: My story
story.lead: From a menu for a game to a product of my own: how I became a design engineer.

omsk.title: It started with a menu for a game
omsk.school: A maths and physics class, plus programming lessons: we wrote websites right in Notepad, in plain HTML, CSS and JS. From the seventh grade I lived in Photoshop, then found Illustrator, and in the eleventh, Figma.
omsk.game: In it I built a menu for a game I played all the time and posted it to the game’s communities. People asked how to install it. Word reached the developers: they offered me a job, then opened my file and stopped answering.
omsk.quote: Over a hundred frames. Not one component.
omsk.after: I was furious at the time. Now I understand them.
omsk.menus: The Figma file of the game menu: dozens of nearly identical screens

university.title: Maths first
university.choice: I wanted to study product design, but a teacher talked me out of it: get your maths up first. So I ended up at Omsk State University, studying applied mathematics and computer science.
university.roles: Programming came easily and I enjoyed it, but in group projects I still ended up as the designer.
university.quote: It’s a pain to check my own class schedule.
university.idea: Some universities had their own apps for that. From 2023 on, my classmate Maxim and I kept talking about building one for ours, and kept putting it off: the idea felt too big.

build.title: VCourse
build.start: In our third year we were given a semester to build a product of our own, and AI had just matured. We went for it. I took product design and the frontend, Maxim the backend and DevOps.
build.learn: I had no experience in mobile development at all. The first semester went on Swift, SwiftUI, Xcode and the iOS guidelines.
build.quote: By the end of the semester my own app was on my phone.
build.polish: The next semester and the summer went into polishing. The app was rewritten from scratch several times: I wanted it to be perfect.
build.layers: The VCourse profile screen in Xcode’s view debugger, pulled apart into layers
build.update: A lock-screen notification: VCourse updated to version 0.1.0
build.icon: The Icon Composer window with an icon of two circles on blue

launch.title: Launch
launch.post: We arranged a post in the university’s Telegram channel. The post went out, and we sat refreshing the pages, watching the numbers.
launch.stageCaption: Presenting VCourse to first-years, as a fourth-year
launch.rankLabel: rank among education apps on the Russian App Store at launch
launch.chartSummary: 632 downloads in the first three days, 411 of them on 2 September.

fork.title: The fork
fork.question: In the semester after the launch, the Android app and the website came out, and five more institutions joined. It all worked, and the question came up: what next? We couldn’t develop it seriously while earning nothing from it.
fork.quote: Ads in the app, or a service for universities.
fork.answer: We really didn’t want ads. We chose the second: our own service for building schedules, with the apps as a pleasant extra for students and teachers. We started talking to the staff who draw up schedules and looking into how it’s really done.
fork.score: A week as a musical score: tangled lines fall into straight rows, with strokes for lessons on them

night.title: One night
night.letter: My bachelor’s was ending and I was looking at master’s programmes in Omsk. One night a newsletter from Central University arrived: a programme in Human Experience Design. In essence, the product design I had wanted to study after school.
night.need: They wanted a portfolio. I had none.
night.quote: I decided not to sleep until I had built something worth sending.
night.wait: The application went out. Then a call, and several weeks of silence.
night.grant: And then a letter: the largest grant they give.

rent.quote: …and now I needed money to rent a flat

moscow.title: Ten prompts
moscow.study: At the end of the summer I moved and started my master’s at Central University.
moscow.job: Alongside that I worked in a team: several iOS app designs a week, plus their ASO. Doing that by hand would have driven me mad.
moscow.agents: I tried agents in Figma. That meant building a whole pipeline, and it worked.
moscow.quote: The tool took the routine. The decisions stayed with me.
moscow.prompts: I won’t claim that an app with icons and an App Store page came out of a single prompt. But I will claim it came out of ten thoughtful prompts, each building on the last.

now.title: A product and a master’s
now.quote: I want to make products where design and code are one job.

open.name: Open to a conversation
open.text: If you need someone who designs and takes it all the way to code, write to me.

pora.name: Pora na Paru
pora.label: My own product · since 2024
pora.text: A schedule service for universities and apps for students. The same lesson lives in the browser, on iPhone and on Android, and I write all three clients myself.

stage.value: alpha testing on iOS and Android, the web is public

clients.value: iOS, Android and the web since 2 June 2026

pora.note: The frames are the product’s real screens with made-up data.

web.title: The week in a browser
web.text: The week of any group, teacher or room via a link, with nothing to install. Live since 16 October 2026.
web.alt: The schedule in a browser: a group’s week on a Monday, with the first lesson under way.

ios.title: The lesson on the lock screen
ios.text: On iPhone the current lesson stays in a Live Activity and the Dynamic Island on its own, switching from lesson to break to the end of the day. The store build has been with testers in TestFlight since 27 September 2026.
ios.alt: An iPhone lock screen with a Live Activity for the current lesson.

android.title: The same lesson on Android
android.text: Built to Android’s rules: the home screen holds favourite groups and teachers, the current lesson and lesson notes, and the lesson is in a widget too. Material 3 Expressive colours. In closed testing on Google Play since 30 September 2026.
android.alt: The Android app’s home screen: favourites, the current lesson and lesson notes.

editor.title: Publishing without clashes
editor.text: An editor for the academic office: a teacher booked for two lessons at once is highlighted before publishing, and a moved lesson reaches every app straight away. The workspace is being designed.
editor.conflict: Clash: Ivanov D.N. in two lessons at once

flow.name: Flow
flow.label: Case study · iOS app production line, 2026
flow.text: How I adapted agents to production-line design: a terminal and a Markdown knowledge base carried each task from brief to finished screens. It was a solution for one kind of work, not my usual process.
flow.note: The task in the demo is made up.

brief.title: Brief
brief.text: The spec became a short brief and a board of six style directions.
brief.me: I picked the style and answered questions
brief.tool: A brief in ten minutes, visual research, a style board
brief.hint: Pick a direction for me: the screens ahead will take its colours.

research.title: Research
research.text: References from real apps, a breakdown of patterns and a map of screens.
research.me: Review, then “go”: stage 2 waited for my word
research.tool: Research, screen map, tokens, wireframes, audit

screens.title: Screens
screens.text: A wireframe became a screen in place: the same frames at the same coordinates.
screens.me: I reviewed the key screens at the checkpoint
screens.tool: Components, onboarding, paywall, main feature, other branches

handoff.title: Handoff
handoff.text: One run produced a file ready for development.
handoff.me: I went through the file, fixed it myself or sent it back
handoff.tool: Prototype, cover, 28 icons, two store listings, assets

projects.name: Projects
projects.label: Beyond the product
projects.text: Two projects of my own: this site and everything I do in LaTeX. On their page they sit on a board, like mockups in a design editor.
projects.themes: Every page declares its theme: colours, typefaces and the look of controls. With two modes, that makes eight combinations. A component reads tokens and knows nothing about themes.
projects.releases: The thesis came out in releases, like software. Each release is a dated tag: GitHub Actions builds the PDF in a container with TeX Live and attaches it to the release.
